form.label: AI Triage Overview
form.description: Triage and incident output pushed by soc/splunk_client.py as sourcetype=ai_triage. Only derived fields are forwarded, so no raw alert payload is searchable here. Untested against a live Splunk instance.

panel.title: Routing breakdown: queued vs paged vs likely benign

search.query: sourcetype=ai_triage action=* analysis_source=$source_filter$ | stats count by action | eval action = case( action=="page_now", "Paged now", action=="queue_review", "Queued for review", action=="mark_likely_benign", "Marked likely benign", true(), action) | sort -count
sourcetype=ai_triage action=* analysis_source=$source_filter$ | timechart span=1h count by action

sourcetype=ai_triage action=* analysis_source=$source_filter$ | eval score_band = case( score >= 8, "8-10 page", score >= 4, "4-7 queue", true(), "1-3 likely benign") | timechart span=1h count by score_band
sourcetype=ai_triage action=* analysis_source=$source_filter$ | stats count by score | sort +score

html.p: A score produced by the deterministic local rules is not the same evidence as a model score, and a failed model call falls back to local scoring. If this panel is mostly local during a run you expected to be model-assisted, the model path is degrading silently.

search.query: sourcetype=ai_triage action=* | eval analysis_source = if(isnull(analysis_source), "unrecorded", analysis_source) | timechart span=1h count by analysis_source

panel.title: Score and action by analysis source

search.query: sourcetype=ai_triage action=* | eval analysis_source = if(isnull(analysis_source), "unrecorded", analysis_source) | stats count as results avg(score) as avg_score count(eval(action=="page_now")) as paged count(eval(action=="mark_likely_benign")) as likely_benign dc(model) as models by analysis_source | eval avg_score = round(avg_score, 2) | sort -results

sourcetype=ai_triage action="page_now" analysis_source=$source_filter$ | table _time target_id target_type score classification fp_likelihood analysis_source model prompt_version summary | sort -_time
sourcetype=ai_triage candidate_count=* | stats count as incidents max(max_score) as worst_score sum(alert_count) as alerts values(primary_user) as users by primary_host | sort -incidents -worst_score
